chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked, 'What is the meaning of the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'The lowest among them ensures the safety of the highest among them'?' He said, 'If an army of Muslims besieged a group of polytheists, and a man from them climbed up (to the walls) and said, 'Give me security so that I may meet your leader and negotiate with him,' and they gave him security, the lowest among them ensures it, and it becomes obligatory upon the highest among them to fulfill it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the validity of security (aman) granted by the lowest-ranking member of a group?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the scope of *aman* (safe conduct) in military jurisprudence, establishing that the guarantee granted by the lowest-ranking individual is binding upon the highest-ranking leader. This principle underscores the collective nature of the truce, ensuring that the security of one member extends to the entire group, thereby preventing arbitrary revocation of safety by superior commanders. It highlights the legal weight of individual agency within a hierarchical structure, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding treaties and prisoner treatment.
